metaDescription: Seven ceiling TV mounts compared on weight rating, pole length, tilt and swivel, VESA range and joist needs, from fixed pole to motorized drop down models.
expertTake: The WALI heavy duty mount is the best overall pick, because a 220 pound rating, a 37 to 90 inch range, an 18 degree downward tilt and a full 360 degree swivel give it the widest margin of any pole mount here. The PEGZONE is the value pick for 43 to 86 inch TVs with a stated 155 pound rating, and the VIVO 10 foot mount is the one for a high or vaulted ceiling. Skip a ceiling mount if you cannot reach a joist or beam, since drywall alone cannot hold the load.
introParagraphs: A ceiling TV mount hangs the screen from a pole attached to the ceiling, which frees wall space and lets you place the TV in a corner, over a bed, in a loft or in a room with windows on every wall. It is the answer when a wall mount is impossible.

The mount is only as good as what it screws into. We evaluated seven mounts on the stated weight rating, pole length, tilt and swivel range and VESA compatibility, and on the practical reality of finding a joist, hiding the cable and getting a heavy screen up there safely.

products.name: WALI Heavy Duty Ceiling TV Mount, 37 to 90 in, up to 220 lb, 18 Degree Tilt, 360 Degree Swivel
products.description:
A heavy duty hanging pole mount for 37 to 90 inch TVs up to 220 pounds, with solid steel construction, an 18 degree downward tilt and a 360 degree swivel. The 220 pound rating is the highest among standard pole mounts here, and it gives a real margin for large TVs that weigh 80 to 120 pounds.

The 18 degree downward tilt is generous, which matters when the TV hangs high and you look up at it from a sofa. The 360 degree swivel lets you rotate the screen toward a bed, a sofa or a kitchen. The tradeoff is weight and size: the mount and a large TV together are a heavy load on the ceiling, so the joist must be solid and the lag bolts correctly sized. Compared with the PEGZONE, it handles bigger and heavier screens.

Find the joists with a stud finder, mark the plate holes and lift the TV with two people. Route cables through the pole and check the safety lock.
products.bestFor: Large TVs that need a strong, tilting, swiveling ceiling mount.

products.name: PEGZONE Ceiling TV Mount, 43 to 86 in, 155 lb, Height 19.1 to 36.4 in, Full Motion

specList.label: Motion
specList.value: Full motion, 180 degree swivel each way

products.description:
A full motion ceiling mount for 43 to 86 inch TVs up to 155 pounds, with a telescoping pole that adjusts from 19.1 to 36.4 inches and 180 degrees of swivel in each direction. The pole range is a clear, stated figure, and it tells you the TV can hang from 19 to 36 inches below the ceiling, which suits a standard 8 to 10 foot ceiling.

A 155 pound rating covers nearly any consumer TV in the 43 to 86 inch range with a margin. The telescoping pole gives you height adjustment without a second pole. Compared with the WALI, it is rated for a lower load but suits the same screen sizes, so for most living rooms it is enough.

Check that the joist is solid, use the supplied bolts and hang the TV with a helper. Set the pole length to bring the screen to eye level when seated.

products.name: VIVO Ceiling TV Mount, 43 to 86 in, 132 lb, Telescoping Height, Fits Sloped Ceilings

specList.label: Ceiling
specList.value: Fits sloped ceilings, tilts up to 90 degrees

products.description:
A telescoping ceiling mount for 43 to 86 inch TVs up to 132 pounds, with a steel and aluminum build and a bracket that tilts up to 90 degrees to fit sloped ceilings. The sloped ceiling feature is the main reason to choose it: a standard flat plate does not sit flush on a vaulted ceiling, and the tilting bracket lets the pole hang straight.

A 132 pound rating suits most TVs in range with a margin, and the telescoping pole adjusts the height. The listing says it covers 43 to 86 inches, so the mount is aimed at mid to large screens. Compared with the PEGZONE, the VIVO has a lower rating but the sloped ceiling fit.

Use a stud finder to find the rafters, check the slope angle and hang the TV with help. Make sure the pole hangs plumb before connecting the TV.

products.name: VIVO 10 ft Extendable Ceiling TV Mount, 37 to 90 in, 110 lb, 98.5 to 118.2 in Drop
products.description:
A 10 foot extendable ceiling mount for 37 to 90 inch TVs up to 110 pounds, with a stated drop of 98.5 to 118.2 inches from the ceiling. This is the mount for a very tall ceiling, such as a loft, a church style room or a commercial space where a normal pole would leave the TV near the ceiling.

A 110 pound rating is modest, and a 90 inch TV can approach that figure, so check the weight of your set. A very long pole also adds sway and leverage on the ceiling fixing, and the longer the pole, the more careful the joist mounting must be. Compared with the WALI, it trades rating for reach.

Use a rafter or a beam and avoid using it on a very light ceiling. Cable management along a 10 foot pole needs ties and a raceway.

products.name: WALI Ceiling TV Mount, 26 to 65 in, up to 110 lb, Hanging Pole, 2 Inch Height Increments
products.description:
A hanging pole ceiling mount for 26 to 65 inch TVs up to 110 pounds with steel and aluminum construction and height adjustment in 2 inch increments. The incremental adjustment is a small design point that matters in practice, since you can set the height precisely without guessing.

A standard pole mount for TVs up to 65 inches covers most bedroom and kitchen sets, and the 110 pound rating is more than enough for a 55 or 65 inch TV. The tradeoff is the size range: it cannot support the bigger screens that the heavy duty and extended mounts can. Compared with the PERLESMITH, the WALI is similar in range and has the added increments.

Use joists and hang the TV with a helper. Tighten the swivel and tilt joints so the screen stays where you set it.

products.name: Mount-It! Ceiling TV Mount, 32 to 75 in, 110 lb, Height Adjustable 22 to 36 in, Full Motion
products.description:
A full motion ceiling mount for 32 to 75 inch TVs up to 110 pounds with 360 degree rotation and a height adjustable pole of 22 to 36 inches. The stated pole range is a useful figure, and the 75 inch limit sits between the standard 65 inch mounts and the large mounts.

The mount is described as built from high strength alloy steel. Its 110 pound rating limits it, since a 75 inch TV can weigh 70 to 100 pounds, so check your TV's weight. Compared with the PEGZONE, the Mount-It has a lower rating and a smaller range.

Install into joists and hang the TV with two people. Keep the pole at the right height so the screen sits at eye level.

products.name: monTEK Motorized Ceiling TV Mount, 37 to 75 in, Remote, App and Voice Control, 0 to 80 Degree Tilt

specList.label: Tilt
specList.value: 0 to 80 degrees, plus or minus 2 degree leveling

products.description:
A motorized ceiling mount for 37 to 75 inch TVs that flips the screen down from the ceiling with a remote, a smartphone app or voice control, with a tilt from 0 to 80 degrees and a plus or minus 2 degree leveling adjustment. This is a different category from a pole mount: the TV folds flat against the ceiling when not in use and drops down on command.

A motorized flip mount hides the TV, which is ideal in a bedroom or a loft where you want a clear ceiling when the screen is off. The tradeoff is motors, wiring and cost: it needs a nearby outlet or a power run, and the motor is a part that can fail. Compared with the pole mounts, it is more expensive and more complex.

Plan the wiring before installation, use rafters for fixing and check the motor limit settings. Keep the remote nearby and update any app firmware.

buyingCriteria.explanation: The rating must exceed the TV weight by at least 25 percent, and a ceiling mount is a hanging load with leverage. Mounts range from 110 pounds, as on the standard WALI, to 220 pounds on the WALI heavy duty. A 75 inch TV can weigh 70 to 100 pounds, so check the weight from the manual, not a guess.

buyingCriteria.criterion: What the ceiling is made of
buyingCriteria.explanation: A ceiling mount must screw into a joist, beam or rafter, never into drywall alone. Find the joists with a stud finder, and check the spacing against the plate. Concrete ceilings need masonry anchors, and suspended tile ceilings cannot take a mount. If you cannot reach a solid structure, do not install.

The pole sets how far the TV hangs. A 19 to 36 inch pole, like the PEGZONE, suits standard 8 to 10 foot ceilings, while a 10 foot extendable pole, like the VIVO, suits very tall ones. Measure the ceiling height and the height you want the screen centre to sit at.

A downward tilt of 15 to 25 degrees helps with a high hang, and a 360 degree swivel serves several viewing spots. The WALI heavy duty tilts down 18 degrees. More motion adds joints that can loosen, so choose what you need.

Check the TV's VESA pattern against the mount plate, for example 400 by 400 or 600 by 400. Some small mounts max out at 400 by 400. A TV may fit by screen size but fail on VESA, especially above 75 inches.
Cables run down the pole, and a long pole needs ties or a raceway. A motorized mount needs a power supply at the ceiling. Plan where the HDMI and power cables run before hanging the TV.

specDecoder.meaning: The maximum TV weight the mount supports, in pounds. Stay at least 25 percent under it.
specDecoder.watchFor: The WALI heavy duty lists 220 lb and several mounts list 110 lb.

specDecoder.meaning: The adjustable drop from the ceiling plate to the TV bracket. It sets how low the screen hangs.
specDecoder.watchFor: The PEGZONE lists 19.1 to 36.4 inches and the VIVO 10 foot lists 98.5 to 118.2 inches.

specDecoder.meaning: The angles the screen can move. Downward tilt aids a high hang and swivel lets you aim the screen.
specDecoder.watchFor: The WALI lists 18 degrees down and 360 degrees of swivel.

specDecoder.meaning: A plate that tilts so the pole hangs straight under a vaulted ceiling.
specDecoder.watchFor: The VIVO 132 lb mount tilts up to 90 degrees.

specDecoder.meaning: A powered mount that folds the TV against the ceiling and drops it on command.
specDecoder.watchFor: The monTEK needs power and wiring at the ceiling.

howWeEvaluated.title: Weight and strength
howWeEvaluated.description: We read each listing for the weight rating, build material and size range. The WALI heavy duty's 220 pound rating and the PEGZONE's 155 pound rating were weighed above vague strength claims. We noted lower ratings for large TVs.

howWeEvaluated.title: Pole and height
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated pole ranges such as 19.1 to 36.4 inches and 98.5 to 118.2 inches against ceiling heights. We noted incremental adjustment. Tall ceilings were matched to the long pole mount.

howWeEvaluated.title: Motion and tilt
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared tilt and swivel ranges, including the 18 degree tilt and the 360 degree swivel. We noted motorized options. More joints were noted as wear points.

howWeEvaluated.title: Installation and ceilings
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at joist needs, sloped ceiling brackets and cable management. The VIVO sloped ceiling bracket scored for flexibility. We noted that no mount works on bare drywall.

howWeEvaluated.title: Owner feedback patterns
howWeEvaluated.description: We researched recurring owner themes on ceiling TV mounts, such as sway, loose joints and joist problems. These patterns shaped the ownership notes. We did not run physical tests, and we do not use star ratings.

cards.label: Pole (WALI, PEGZONE)
cards.text: Simple, strong and reliable. The TV stays visible and hangs at a fixed height.

cards.label: Motorized (monTEK)
cards.text: Hides the TV and drops it on command. More wiring, a motor to maintain and a higher cost.

howToChoose.note: Choose a pole for simplicity and a motorized mount for a hidden screen.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A tilt of 18 degrees or more, a swivel to face the bed and a rating well above the TV weight. A motorized flip keeps the ceiling clear.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The WALI heavy duty and the monTEK fit bedrooms best. The PEGZONE suits mid size TVs.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: The TV is large and heavy or hangs from a tall ceiling. A higher rating and a better build give a safer hang.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: The TV is under 55 inches in a standard room. A basic pole mount covers it.

maintenance.why: Vibration and load can loosen bolts. A check keeps the TV secure.

maintenance.task: Check the pole joints and swivel
maintenance.why: Joints loosen with movement. Tighten them so the screen holds position.
Cables can pull or sag along a long pole. Re-tie and re-route if needed.
Dust collects on the top of a hanging TV. A dry cloth keeps it clean.
Motors and remotes fail over time. Test the limit stops and batteries.

faq.q: Can I mount a TV from the ceiling on drywall?
faq.a: No. You must fix into a joist, beam or rafter. Drywall alone cannot hold the load.

faq.q: How low should the TV hang?
faq.a: The screen centre should sit at eye level when seated, about 40 to 42 inches from the floor. Set the pole length to match.
Long poles sway more than short ones. A solid joist mount and tight joints reduce it.

faq.q: Can I use one on a vaulted ceiling?
faq.a: Yes, with a sloped ceiling bracket. Check the angle and find the rafters.

faq.q: How heavy a TV can I hang?
faq.a: Stay at least 25 percent under the mount's rating. A 75 inch TV can weigh 70 to 100 pounds.
They work well but add motors and wiring. Check power access and keep the remote handy.
